mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which tends to boost equity markets by reducing borrowing costs and increasing risk appetite.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 60% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS levels, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 5% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as investor sentiment deteriorates.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following a UNRATE increase above 5%, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) is strong but unemployment (UNRATE) is high, it indicates labor market inefficiencies, which can lead to negative S&P 500 returns due to economic uncertainty.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 55% of the 60-day windows following such labor market conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, high federal funds rates increase borrowing costs, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are pressured.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows during a monetary tightening cycle, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Strong real sales (RSAFS) indicate robust consumer demand, which supports corporate revenues and leads to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 5-day windows following strong RSAFS growth, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals strong economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 returns as production and earnings grow.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 45% of the 60-day windows following an INDPRO increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) is strong but federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) are high, it indicates inflationary pressures, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as tighter monetary policy may follow.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following such conditions, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion, low unemployment (UNRATE) indicates a tight labor market, which can lead to wage inflation and positive S&P 500 returns as companies invest in growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows during a late-cycle expansion, the hypothesis is rejected.
